messages:
maya: Quick brain dump — I'm prototyping a different attribution model for cache savings: rolling "delta-buckets" per billing window instead of fully amortizing per-session. Aim is more stable per-tenant previews in the console and fewer surprises on invoices.

ben: Can you sketch the difference? shorter please :)

maya: Sure — current model: when a prefetch hits, we attach the full future-token savings to the originating session which gets amortized across the tenant. Problem: large multi-step sessions create big spikes. New idea: split cache saves into fixed-duration buckets (eg 1h) and record deltas per SKU. That way the console can preview per-window savings and we can apply fallback heuristics deterministically.

ryan: Sounds promising. How do we avoid double-counting when cached tokens are used across tenants (shared cache)?

maya: Two pieces: 1) attribution by origin hash: deterministic hash(invocation_id) % N => partition — makes assignment idempotent and stable without storing per-request state. 2) when cross-tenant sharing is detected, we prorate by observed hit-likelihood per tenant in same bucket (sampling).

sophia: Sampling worries me for billing accuracy. What's the sampling rate and error bounds?

maya: Prototype uses 5% sampled invocations with bootstrapped confidence intervals. For SKUs with low volume we fall back to conservative rounding up. The goal is auditability + low compute.

samir: What does the API look like for this? we need an internal shape for ops and console to consume (and tests).

maya: Draft API shape:
```
POST /internal/econ/credits/apply
{
  "tenant_id": "t-123",
  "window_start": 1714123200,
  "window_end": 1714126799,
  "strategy": "delta-buckets-v1",
  "entries": [
    {"sku": "open-3b-q8_0", "tokens_saved": 12345, "partition_key": "p-42"},
    {"sku": "redwood-7b-q4", "tokens_saved": 543, "partition_key": "p-42"}
  ]
}
```
This is intentionally lightweight — no per-invocation blobs. partition_key is the deterministic hash bucket.

ben: Console UX: we'd want a "Preview window" toggle and a diff slider (last 24h / prior 24h) so finance can see the delta. Also a small explainer: "delta-buckets attribution — rolling 1h windows" that links to docs.

sophia: Also need a flag to disable this for certain tenants (enterprise legal asks). Add `control_plane.disable_delta_buckets=true` to tenant profile?

maya: Yep — will add tenant opt-out via our feature flags service.

ryan: Two infra concerns: 1) recomputing proration requires access to cross-tenant hit matrices — heavy. 2) sampling introduces skew if distribution changes rapidly. Any mitigation?

maya: For 1) we only compute proration when shared-hit rate > threshold (0.5% of hits in window). Otherwise treat as single-owner. For 2) use rolling bootstrap windows and surface a confidence score to the console; if confidence < 0.7, show "estimate" badge and optionally switch to conservative attribution.

samir: How will this interact with routing fallback policies / quotas? Example: tenant A gets routed to cheaper SKU then fallback to more expensive model — credits need to be associated with route+sku so we don't subsidize wrong routing decisions.
